comments.body:
ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS (rebar-debug protocol, fresh worktree @ origin/main) — NOT A BUG. The reported premise ("show omits persisted outbound links / stale read") is REFUTED by direct observation; all three candidate defects classify as misunderstanding or intended-behavior.

H1 — "show does not reflect the LINK event" : REFUTED (misunderstanding).
Ground truth, production store: `rebar show viral-peppy-lowchen` returns deps: [{target_id: 3211-be4f-d4aa-4b5c, relation: discovered_from, link_uuid: f30a6c94-…}] AND status: idea in the SAME read — the LINK event (16:06:52) and the later STATUS event (16:06:57) are BOTH folded. There is no `links` key in show's JSON and never has been; the observing agent inspected d.get('links') and concluded "no links" from a key that does not exist. Reproduced end-to-end in a scratch store: link A→B discovered_from, then show A → edge present under `deps`; show B → edge present under `inbound_deps`. No reducer fold gap, no cache staleness — reducer/_processors.py process_link folds LINK into the source's deps.
AUTHORITY: docs/ticket-model.md §"Direction and visibility": "A link is stored one-sided on the source ticket's record (`deps`: outgoing edges only). `show` additionally renders the computed `inbound_deps` list…". No schema, help text, or doc promises a `links` key (grep of src/rebar/schemas/, _cli/help/, docs/ — zero hits).

H2 — "`rebar link` success prints nothing" : CONFIRMED behavior, classified intended-behavior.
Dynamic proof (scratch store): first link → exit 0, 0 bytes stdout. Static: _commands/link_revert.py link_cli returns 0 with no success print (only errors, --dry-run previews, and hierarchy-REDIRECT records are printed). Convention census, run live: comment, tag, unlink, and transition are ALL equally silent on success (exit 0, empty stdout). Only create/revert print — they return generated identifiers the caller cannot otherwise know. Silence-on-success is the uniform repo-wide CLI convention for mutations against known ids (Unix convention), not a link-specific gap.

H3 — "re-link identical edge: exit 0, no event, no 'already linked' notice" : CONFIRMED, classified intended-behavior (silent idempotent no-op by design).
Dynamic proof: re-ran identical link in scratch store → exit 0, empty stdout+stderr, LINK-file count unchanged (1 before, 1 after).
AUTHORITY: graph/_links.py add_dependency docstring: "Idempotent: if a net-active LINK with the same (target_id, relation) already exists, this is a no-op (exits cleanly without writing a duplicate event)." The _is_active_link guard carries bug-fix pedigree (f5a8 SNAPSHOT-compaction fallback) proving the idempotency is deliberately maintained design, not an accident. Post-state after a duplicate link is identical to success — the edge exists — so exit 0 is truthful. An "already linked" notice would be a UX feature-request, not a defect.

H4 — "enrich-drain WARNING masked/displaced the success output" : REFUTED.
rebar's logging installs a stderr handler (_cli/__init__.py:439-444, install_stderr_handler). The observed invocation ran `2>&1 | tail -1`, merging stderr into stdout; tail -1 showed the warning because it was the ONLY line — link's success stdout is empty by design (H2). Nothing was eaten or displaced.

CAUSAL CHAIN of the incident: agent linked (persisted, silent success per convention) → read show via a nonexistent `links` key → falsely concluded the write failed → retried → designed idempotent no-op (silent, exit 0) → filed this ticket on the stale-read premise.

DEFECT LEGITIMACY: misunderstanding (H1, the actual trigger) + intended-behavior (H2/H3/H4). Per the not-a-bug guard, NO fix is written.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION: (1) keep this comment as the corrected account; (2) edit the description to replace the refuted stale-read framing with the corrected account (retitle accordingly); (3) close with an administrative/not-a-bug class once that close-class machinery lands — do not force-close; (4) if the UX ideas are wanted (an "already linked" stderr notice on idempotent re-link; a documented pointer that outbound links live under `deps`), file them as separate feature/docs tickets linked discovered_from this one — they are enhancements, not defects. Note the acceptance criteria on this ticket are already 3/4 satisfied by current behavior (show DOES surface both directions; LINK+STATUS both fold; re-link writes no duplicate) — only the notice text is new work.

compiled_state.description:
## Corrected account (post-RCA): NOT A BUG
Original premise (stale link read) REFUTED by rebar-debug investigation — see the RCA comment for full evidence.

What actually happened: after `rebar link viral-peppy-lowchen creatable-foldable-arthropods discovered_from`, the LINK event persisted immediately (event f30a6c94, 16:06:52.581) and `rebar show` DID return it in the same read that showed the later STATUS event — under the documented `deps` key (docs/ticket-model.md §"Direction and visibility": `deps` = outgoing, `inbound_deps` = inbound). The observing agent queried a nonexistent `links` key and misread the empty default as a missing write.

Per-hypothesis verdicts:
- H1 show omits LINK: refuted — misunderstanding (edge present in `deps`; no contract promises `links`).
- H2 silent success: intended-behavior — Unix convention across comment/tag/unlink/transition (only create/revert print, they return generated ids).
- H3 silent idempotent re-link: intended-behavior — add_dependency docstring pins the idempotent no-op; guard has bug-fix pedigree (f5a8). An "already linked" notice would be a feature request.
- H4 enrich-drain WARNING masking stdout: refuted — logs are stderr; success stdout is empty by design.

Disposition: closed not_a_bug. No code change warranted; 3 of the original 4 acceptance criteria are already satisfied by current behavior.
